title: Finite free algebra norm and primes over a prime
statement: Let R and S be commutative rings, with S a finite free R-algebra. Let p be a prime ideal of R, and a an element of S. The algebra norm N_{S/R}(a) lies outside p if and only if a lies outside every prime ideal q of S whose contraction to R is p. The algebra may have rank zero; no domain, constant positive rank, or field hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Use the already proved Algebra.norm_notMem_iff from WeilConjectures.Mathlib.RingTheory.Localization.NormTrace. Its proof localizes R at p and S at the image of the complement of p. Norms commute with this localization, and an element of a finite free algebra is a unit exactly when its norm is a unit (the inverse multiplication endomorphism gives an inverse element by evaluation at 1). Thus the norm avoids p exactly when the localized element is a unit. Such a unit avoids every prime over p: those primes extend to proper primes of the localization. Conversely, a nonunit lies in a maximal ideal of the localization. Its contraction q0 to S contracts into p. Since S is integral over R, going up produces a prime q containing q0 with contraction p; q contains a. This contradicts avoidance of all primes over p. In rank zero the norm is 1 and S has no primes, so both conditions hold.

theorem norm_notMem_iff [Module.Free R S] [Module.Finite R S] (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime]
    (a : S) : Algebra.norm R a ∉ p ↔
      ∀ q : Ideal S, q.IsPrime → q.comap (algebraMap R S) = p → a ∉ q
